translationRepairs: "Surely no one loves you more than the crown prince," Deng Tong said."
“Surely no one loves you more than the crown prince,” Deng Tong said.

Focus unit 通曰：「宜莫若太子。」 is a single reported speech followed by the reporting clause; the prior idiomatic string ends with an extra closing quotation mark after said, which is a real punctuation error. The proposed repair removes that stray mark and leaves the sense unchanged.
The senior princess shuttled messages to the empress dowager's residence.
He acted as intermediary, carrying messages back and forth to the Eastern Palace.

In 長主往來通語東宮, surrounding units name 長 as the same actor (帝嘉長義; 追顯長前功; 侍中衛尉長), so 長 is Chunyu Chang and 主 is the verb “take charge,” not the compound 長主 “senior princess.” The proposed idiomatic repair restores that agent and action without inventing content.
The senior princess went back and forth conveying words to the eastern palace.
He took charge of going back and forth to convey messages to the Eastern Palace.

The same focus phrasing 長主往來通語東宮 must be segmented as Chang taking charge of the back-and-forth messaging to the Eastern Palace; the prior literal invents an unmentioned senior princess. The proposed literal matches the Chinese agents and verbs.

More than a year later Empress Zhao was installed, and the emperor, deeply grateful, recalled Wang Chang's earlier service. He issued an edict: "Former Director of Works Xie Wannian memorialized requesting construction at Changling, exhausting the empire. Palace Attendant and Defender of the Capital Wang Chang repeatedly stated that the work should stop and that relocated households should be returned to their former homes. I referred Chang's words to the dukes and ministers, and all who deliberated agreed with his plan.

More than a year later Empress Zhao was installed, and the emperor, deeply grateful, recalled Chunyu Chang's earlier service. He issued an edict: "Former Director of Works Xie Wannian memorialized requesting construction at Changling, exhausting the empire. Palace Attendant and Defender of the Capital Chunyu Chang repeatedly stated that the work should stop and that relocated households should be returned to their former homes. I referred Chang's words to the dukes and ministers, and all who deliberated agreed with his plan.

Focus unit names only 長 (and titles 侍中衛尉長) in Chunyu Chang’s biography; “Wang Chang” is an invented surname not present in 追顯長前功 or the edict’s 侍中衛尉長. Replacing both occurrences with Chunyu Chang corrects the naming error while leaving the rest of the English intact.
"Go to the empress dowager at once," Wang Gen ordered."
“Go to the empress dowager at once,” Wang Gen ordered.

Focus unit 根曰：「趣白東宮。」 is one quoted command plus a reporting clause; the prior idiomatic string adds a stray closing quotation mark after ordered. Removing that mark fixes a real error without changing meaning.
Kong Guang, ever correct, knew the point was to humiliate him: he waited at his gate in full dress, then slipped back inside the moment Dong Xian's carriage appeared.
Kong Guang, ever correct, knew the sovereign wished to exalt Dong Xian: he waited at his gate in full dress, then slipped back inside the moment Dong Xian's carriage appeared.

Focus unit 知上欲尊寵賢 states that Kong Guang knew the sovereign wished to honor and favor Dong Xian; “knew the point was to humiliate him” reverses that motive. The proposed clause restores 上欲尊寵賢 accurately and keeps the waiting-at-the-gate narrative.
Hong had native shrewdness; hearing Xian's words he too understood, returned and reported to Gong, conveying in depth Xian's meaning of self-deprecation.
Hong had native shrewdness; hearing Xiao Xian's words he too understood, returned and reported to Gong, conveying in depth Xiao Xian's meaning of self-deprecation.

Focus unit 聞咸言……深達咸自謙薄之意 uses 咸 (Xiao Xian), contrasting with Dong Xian’s 賢 elsewhere; bare “Xian” in the prior literal risks misattributing the speech. Specifying Xiao Xian for both 咸 references is the accurate disambiguation.

When he arrived, by the empress dowager's order she had the secretariat impeach Xian for not personally overseeing medicine when the emperor was ill, and forbade Xian from entering or leaving the palace compound.

When Wang Mang arrived, acting on the empress dowager's instruction, he had the secretariat impeach Dong Xian for failing to oversee the emperor's medicine personally during his illness, and forbade Xian from entering or leaving the palace compound.

Preceding 太后遣使者召莽 makes Mang the arriver in 既至; 以太后指使尚書劾賢 means he, acting on the dowager’s direction, had the secretariat impeach Xian. The prior literal’s “she had” wrongly makes the dowager the agent of 使; the proposal correctly keeps Mang as agent.
Deng Tong of Nan'an in Shu had been a Yellow-Turban boatman in the imperial service.
Deng Tong of Nan'an in Shu had been a Yellow-Head boatman in the imperial service.
黃頭郎 is the yellow-capped boat service, not the Yellow Turbans (黃巾); the idiomatic English imports a later rebel movement.

Emperor Wen once dreamed he wished to ascend to heaven but could not; there was a Yellow-Turban Gentleman who pushed him up, and when he looked back he saw the seam at the back of the man's trousers was worn through.

Emperor Wen once dreamed he wished to ascend to heaven but could not; there was a Yellow-Head Gentleman who pushed him up, and when he looked back he saw the seam at the back of the man's trousers was worn through.
The dream figure is 黃頭郎, the same yellow-head boat gentleman as Deng Tong, not a Yellow-Turban Gentleman.
Han Yan, styled Wangsun, was grandson of Marquis of Gonggao Kui Dang.
Han Yan, styled Wangsun, was grandson of Marquis of Gonggao Tuidang.
弓高侯穨當 is Marquis of Gonggao Tuidang; Kui Dang misreads the personal name 穨當.
Han Yan, courtesy name Wangsun, was the grandson of Marquis of Gonggao Kui Dang.
Han Yan, courtesy name Wangsun, was the grandson of Marquis of Gonggao Tuidang.
The literal likewise misreads 穨當 as Kui Dang; Tuidang restores the name.
Humiliated, the king wept to the empress dowager and asked to return to his kingdom or to enter palace guard duty, to be treated like Han Yan.
Humiliated, the king wept to the empress dowager and asked to return his kingdom and enter palace guard duty, to be treated like Han Yan.
請得歸國入宿衛，比韓嫣 is one request to relinquish the kingdom and enter palace guard service like Han Yan, not an or-choice between going home and joining the guard.
When Lady Li bore the king of Changyi, he was made director of harmony with a two-thousand-picul seal, shared the emperor's intimacy, and matched Han Yan in favor.
When Lady Li bore the king of Changyi, Yannian was made director of harmony with a two-thousand-picul seal, shared the emperor's intimacy, and matched Han Yan in favor.
延年由是貴為協律都尉 names Li Yannian as the one promoted; bare 'he' after 產昌邑王 wrongly points to the newborn king.
Matters large and small were decided on white slips through Xian; he was so honored and favored that he tilted the whole court, and the hundred officials all treated Xian with respect.
Matters large and small were reported through Xian and decided; he was so honored and favored that he tilted the whole court, and the hundred officials all treated Xian with respect.
因顯白決 means matters were reported through Xian and then decided, not decided on 'white slips'.

Seeing General of the Left Feng Fengshi and his sons prominent at court—and a daughter already a favored lady—Shi Xian tried to curry favor by recommending her brother, Usher Jun, as fit for inner service.

Seeing General of the Left Feng Fengshi and his sons prominent at court—and a daughter already a Zhaoyi in the inner palace—Shi Xian tried to curry favor by recommending her brother, Usher Jun, as fit for inner service.
昭儀在內 is the consort rank Zhaoyi inside the palace, not a generic favored lady.
Late in Yuan's reign the emperor fell ill; King Gong of Dingtao was the favored choice, and Shi Xian's backing of the crown prince carried real weight.
Late in Yuan's reign the emperor fell ill; King Gong of Dingtao was beloved and favored, and Shi Xian's backing of the crown prince carried real weight.
定陶恭王愛幸 describes King Gong as personally beloved and favored; 太子 is a separate person whom Shi Xian backed, so 'favored choice' wrongly fuses them.
After Yuan died and Chengdi took the throne, Shi Xian was shunted to Director of Palace Servants at Changxin Palace on a salary of two thousand shi.
After Yuan died and Chengdi took the throne, Shi Xian was transferred to Director of Palace Servants at Changxin Palace, rank fully two thousand shi.
遷 is a transfer, and 秩中二千石 is the fully-two-thousand-shi grade, not ordinary two-thousand-shi salary.
The empress dowager also angrily said: "The son has come to this!
The empress dowager also angrily said: "Has the boy come to this!
太后’s 兒 is a junior relative (Chunyu Chang), not her own son; 'the boy' matches 兒 without inventing that kinship.
His father Gong was an imperial secretary; on Gong's recommendation Xian became gentleman of the household to the heir apparent.
His father Gong was an imperial secretary; by Gong's privilege of appointment Xian became gentleman of the household to the heir apparent.
任賢為太子舍人 is the Han yin privilege of placing a son in office, not a recommendation; the proposed parenthetical (yin/任) is accurate but unnatural in the literal English.
To spare him trips home, Ai let Dong Xian's wife carry palace passes and live in his lodge inside, as if she were quartered in a ministry hostel.
To spare him trips home, Ai let Dong Xian's wife carry palace passes and live in his lodge inside, like an official's wife and children quartered in a ministry hostel.

若吏妻子居官寺捨 includes 子 (children) omitted in the original, but 'as if she were an official's wife and children' is ungrammatical; the simile should compare the lodging arrangement, not identify the wife as both.

The general's younger male cousin by patriline, palace attendant and chief commandant of the imperial convoy Wu, and his clansman senior by generation, left aide colonel of garrison cavalry Xuan, both knew of Hong's and Xudan's kinship ties to marquises, kings, and empresses—yet Xuan appointed Dan as imperial household subordinate, Wu had thick dealings with Hong and repeatedly praised and recommended Hong.

The general's younger male cousin by patriline, palace attendant and chief commandant of the imperial convoy Wu, and his clansman senior by generation, left aide colonel of garrison cavalry Xuan, both knew of Hong's and Xu Dan's kinship ties to marquises, kings, and queens—yet Xuan appointed Dan as imperial household subordinate; Wu had thick dealings with Hong and repeatedly praised and recommended Hong.
栩丹 is the two-character name Xu Dan, and 諸侯王后 are consorts of feudal kings, not empresses; the fused 'Xudan' and 'empresses' are both wrong.
The following year the Chanyu visited Chang'an for a state banquet with the full court arrayed.
The following year the Chanyu came to court for a banquet audience, with the assembled ministers present.
匈奴單于來朝，宴見 names a court banquet audience; Chang'an is not in the Chinese.

The Wangs who had dominated under Chengdi were spent; only Wang Quji, son of Marquis Tan of Ping'a, who had been Ai's study companion as heir, rose with him to palace attendant and commandant of cavalry.

The Wangs who had dominated under Chengdi were spent; only Wang Quji, son of Marquis Tan of Ping'a, who had won favor as a shuzi cadet while Ai was heir apparent, rose with him to palace attendant and commandant of cavalry.
為庶子得幸 names the heir-household office 庶子, not a study companion.

Mang also prompted Grand Minister of Education Kong Guang to memorialize: "Xian's nature was crafty and fawning; he winged treachery to win a marquisate; father and son monopolized the court, brothers shared favor together; they received vast gifts, built mansions and tombs, aped the limitless style of kings, not differing from royal institutions, the expense reckoned in the hundred millions and emptying the state.

Mang also prompted Grand Minister over the Masses Kong Guang to memorialize: "Xian's nature was crafty and fawning; he winged treachery to win a marquisate; father and son monopolized the court, brothers shared favor together; they received vast gifts, built mansions and tombs, aped the limitless style of kings, not differing from royal institutions, the expense reckoned in the hundred millions and emptying the state.
大司徒 is Grand Minister over the Masses, not Minister of Education.
Chang'an commoners mobbed the Dong gate wailing until the crowd nearly rioted for plunder.
Chang'an commoners clamored in uproar, flocked to his mansion to weep, and the tumult nearly turned to looting.
鄉其第哭 is weeping toward his mansion (第), not a 'Dong gate'.
Zhu Xu of Pei, once a Dong Xian client, resigned from the grand marshal's staff, bought a coffin, and gave Dong Xian a secret burial.
Zhu Xu of Pei, an officer Dong Xian had favored, resigned from the grand marshal's staff, bought a coffin and shroud, collected Dong Xian's corpse, and buried him.

賢所厚吏 is an officer Dong Xian had favored, and 買棺衣收賢屍葬之 is buying coffin and shroud, collecting the corpse, and burying it; 'client' and 'secret burial' are invented and the shroud and recovery are omitted.
Wang Mang, enraged, found another pretext and had Zhu Xu executed.
Wang Mang, enraged, found another pretext and had Zhu Xu beaten to death.
擊殺 is killing by beating; 'executed' flattens the stated manner of death.

When Ai died in a night, a usurper seized the brush; Dong Xian died on a rope, the Ding and Fu clans were swept into exile, and even the dowager paid for misrule—the price of filling office from the pillow instead of from virtue.

When Ai died in a night, treacherous ministers arrogated the mandate; Dong Xian died on a rope, the Ding and Fu clans were swept into exile, and even the dowager paid for misrule—the price of filling office from the pillow instead of from virtue.
奸臣擅命 is treacherous ministers arrogating the mandate, not a usurper seizing a brush.
